_readme: Shared SpriteCook manifest for the Kamigotchi team. All paths are relative to the repo root. AI agents: follow agent_instructions.
SpriteCook asset IDs belong to the account that uploaded or generated them, and SpriteCook only accepts IDs you own as references. So every ID is stored under asset_ids.<account>.
To use this with your own SpriteCook account: upload each style_references[*].source file (pixel=true), add your new ID under asset_ids.<your-name>, and use the presets below with your own IDs.
presets[*].style_references names the style_references category to pass as style_asset_ids. palettes[*] is passed as colors.

Workflow: sketch with quality=low (2 credits), then edit the chosen sketch with edit_asset_id at the preset's quality. Upload small sprites at 8x nearest-neighbour, and afterwards snap the result to native size and the palette.
edits[*].output files marked in_repo=false are local working files that are not committed; only their name and fingerprint are recorded.

agent_instructions.read_first: Instructions for AI agents (Claude Code etc.) working with SpriteCook on Kamigotchi. Follow them exactly. This repo is open source: everything written to it is public.
hard_rules: Never write prompts into the repo: no prompt text, style/theme strings or descriptive edit notes. In this file record only settings, labels, file names, sha12, credits, made_with and status.
No personal absolute paths. Use repo-relative paths; files that are not committed are recorded by file name with in_repo=false.
Asset IDs are per account: SpriteCook only accepts reference IDs owned by the logged-in account. Store them under asset_ids.<github-name> and only use the current user's IDs.
Never overwrite repo art. Save every result as a new versioned file (<name>-v2.png, -v3, ...) outside packages/, unless the user explicitly asks to place a final into the repo.
Never print or save upload tokens or upload URLs.
Check credits (get_credit_balance) and state a job's cost before running it. Use variations=1.
Prefer free local edits (recolours, removing pixels, pasting regions back, restoring original areas) with Python. Only use SpriteCook when new content has to be drawn.
setup_per_teammate: Install the SpriteCook Claude Code plugin: run '/plugin marketplace add SpriteCook/claude-plugin', then '/plugin install spritecook@spritecook', restart Claude Code and sign in to SpriteCook when asked (or via /mcp). Confirm with get_credit_balance. Also install Pillow for the clean-up script (pip install pillow).
Ask for the user's GitHub name; it is their account key.
list_projects; if there is no 'Kamigotchi' project, create_project(name='Kamigotchi'). Record it under accounts.<github-name>.spritecook_project.

For every style_references entry: check that sha256(source)[:12] == sha12 (tell the user if not); create_asset_upload(file_name, content_type='image/png', display_name=label, project_id, pixel=true); PUT the bytes to upload_url with the returned Content-Type (expect 200, print nothing else); finalize_asset_upload(upload_token); store the asset_id under asset_ids.<github-name>. Uploads cost 0 credits.
Optional: save_private_preset for one preset (the free plan allows only 1). The presets in this file work without it.
resolving_presets: style_asset_ids = the current user's IDs for the category named in the preset's style_references (marketing lists specific labels).
colors = the palettes.<category> list; for backgrounds and edits use the original image's own colours.
Copy width, height, aspect_ratio, bg_mode, smart_crop, model, resolution and quality as given. Always pass the user's Kamigotchi project_id.
Native sizes: items 24x24 (some 36x36), skills 24x24, NPCs about 58x112, room backgrounds 128x128.
Use gpt-image-2 (2K is cheaper than 1K). Never use GPT 2.5 Flare/Sunburst with style references (8 credits per reference image).
workflow_new_asset: Read the preset, check credits, tell the user the cost.
Sketch: generate_game_art with the preset but quality='low' (2 credits), wait_seconds=90, and follow the poll contract if it is not finished.
Download, clean up, and show the user at a whole-number zoom with nearest-neighbour scaling (never blurred).
If approved: upload the cleaned sketch at 8x, then generate_game_art(edit_asset_id=<that upload>, quality=<preset quality>). Never spend a high-quality job on an unapproved composition.

Clean up: python3 scripts/art/spritecook_cleanup.py raw.png out.png --size WxH --palette <items|skills|npcs> --remove-bg (sprites need transparency and gpt-image-2 has none; skip --remove-bg for opaque art like skill icons and backgrounds). Add --keep-black if #30111c is wanted on purpose.
Log the result in this file.
workflow_edit_existing: Room backgrounds come in three phase variants, the same drawing in three palettes: backgrounds/playtest-a.png = Daylight, playtest-b.png = Evenfall, playtest-c.png = Moonside (see the room's index.ts; Room.tsx picks backgrounds[phase-1]). Edit ONE phase (usually the one the user chose), then produce the other two locally and for free: python3 scripts/art/spritecook_cleanup.py <edited.png> <out.png> --phase-from <original of the edited phase> --phase-to <original of the target phase>. Show all three side by side. Check for colours that mean different things in different places (for example lake vs roof): any wrong pixels are fixed locally.

After converting, objects whose colours are shared with water or sky (roofs, wood, highlights) can still pick up the wrong phase colour. Trace each object's outline and recolour pixels inside it using how that object is coloured in the target phase's original; trace separate pieces separately so gaps between them stay background.
Make an 8x copy (scripts/art/spritecook_cleanup.py <original> up_x8.png --upscale 8) and upload it. 8x uploads give the correct output size and far less colour drift.
Edit with edit_asset_id, native width/height and colors = the original's palette. For backgrounds use bg_mode='include' and smart_crop=false. Start with quality='low'.
In the edit request, name the single change and explicitly list what must stay exactly the same; one change per job. Never store the request text in the repo.

gpt-image-2 repaints the whole image, so keep only the edited regions: cleanup script with --original <original> --keep-box x0,y0,x1,y1 (repeatable); for irregular regions build a pixel mask in Python. Verify that pixels outside the edit are identical to the source.
Show the user a nearest-neighbour side-by-side (original vs new, 3-4x). Each new request starts from the latest approved version.
Do fine-tuning locally instead of spending credits.
verification_checklist: Output size equals native size (SpriteCook width/height are only hints).
Every pixel is in the palette (colors is only a suggestion to the model; snapping is required).
New black lines (#30111c) are recoloured to #573359 (the script does this by default).
Untouched areas are identical to the source (edits).
Sprites that are transparent in the game come out with a transparent background (the script warns if --remove-bg is missing).

Room edits: all three phase backgrounds (playtest-a/b/c) are delivered and line up pixel for pixel. Compare every edited object with the same object in that phase's original (leaves, roofs, water, foam must use that phase's colours for that object), and fix wrong pixels locally.
logging: edit_sources entry: {label, asset_ids:{<github-name>:id}, source (repo-relative or file name), in_repo, sha12}.

edits entry: {label, edit_of or derived_from, quality, credits, made_with, asset_ids, outputs:[{file, in_repo, sha12}], status}. Status is one of current|superseded|rejected|partly kept, with exactly one current per edited image.
No prompts and no descriptive notes. Update costs.as_of if prices are re-checked.
Before finishing: the file is valid JSON and contains no /home/ paths.
known_spritecook_behaviour: Without an 8x upload, a 128x128 edit came back at 272x278 with about 30,000 colours.
The free plan allows 1 saved preset and 1 job at a time. Uploads are free. No storage limits are published.
The SpriteCook ToS license covers storing and processing uploads 'to provide and improve the Service': upload only what a task needs, not the whole game.
A low-quality edit plus local clean-up is usually enough for small sprites and 128x128 backgrounds.

xenofluxx.note: Free plan: only 1 saved SpriteCook preset, so the other presets live only in this file.

palettes._note: Top 64 colours per category by how many sprites use them (whole folder, not just refs).

presets._note: generate_game_art settings per category (technical only; prompts are not stored in this public file). Finals use the preset's quality; sketch first with quality=low (2 credits), then edit the chosen sketch with edit_asset_id. Only kamigotchi-items is also saved in SpriteCook (free plan allows 1 saved preset).

kamigotchi-backgrounds.colors: palette of the original room image
kamigotchi-backgrounds.upload: edit source uploaded at 8x nearest-neighbour (1024x1024) via scripts/art/spritecook_cleanup.py --upscale 8
kamigotchi-backgrounds.postprocess: postprocess (snap to the original's size and palette, keep_box the edited regions)

steps: Upload edit sources at 8x nearest-neighbour: --upscale 8 (gives correct output size and far less colour drift).
Resize the result to native size with nearest-neighbour and snap every pixel to the palette: --original <source.png> (or --size WxH --colors ...).

Sprites on a solid background: --remove-bg makes the background connected to the image border transparent (skipped automatically if the edge is already transparent). --palette <name> reads a palette from this file.
gpt-image-2 repaints the whole image, so keep the original everywhere except the edited regions: --keep-box x0,y0,x1,y1 (repeatable).
New pure-black pixels (#30111c) are recoloured to the outline purple #573359 automatically (--keep-black to skip).
Check: output size equals native size, colour count stays within the palette, no semi-transparent pixels.

Room phases: --phase-from <edited phase original> --phase-to <target phase original> converts a finished edit to another phase. Unedited pixels are copied exactly from the target original. Thin edited details (highlights, roof tiles, specks; anything not part of a solid 3x3 block of its colour) are recoloured by context, i.e. how the same colour next to the same neighbouring colours is drawn in the originals, because one colour can split into several in another phase (Evenfall orange = Daylight leaf green or lake blue). Larger areas follow connected or nearby unedited pixels. About 98% accurate on hidden blocks. Always review the result against the target original.

style_rules: Native size, no upscaling, no anti-aliasing, no semi-transparent pixels.
New outlines, cracks and lines use #573359, never black.
Tree leaves use the original canopy colours only: #4d6963 with #eb9465 / #bd685b highlights, #573359 for outlines and cluster lines; no bright green #5d995c.

costs.note: 2K is cheaper than 1K on gpt-image-2. GPT 2.5 Flare/Sunburst add 8 credits per reference image. Uploads cost 0. Re-check with list_generation_models before big batches.
